payload.title: Night City Debt
payload.blurb: Night City, 2077. Six million people live in a concrete cage between the Pacific and the Badlands. The megacorps own everything above the twentieth floor, and the gangs own everything below it. You are a nobody in Watson, and the fixer who fed you jobs cut you loose after the last one went…
payload.overview: Night City sits on the Pacific coast, six million people packed between the water and the Badlands, a desert of dead towns and gang roads outside the city limits. Arasaka and Militech own the towers above the twentieth floor, and everything they run depends on people who live below it. Down there the gangs run the streets: Maelstrom with its chrome clinics and chop shops, the Valentinos with their garages and clubs, the Tyger Claws, 6th Street and the rest. Watson is the old working district downtown, where noodle carts, clinics and flophouses sit under the expressways. Westbrook is the rich district of glass and private lawns, where the money goes to sleep. Pacifica is a ruin the city gave up on. Cyberware is cheap to buy and expensive to keep, and every implant is paid for in installments, favors or blood. Fixers take jobs from the corps and the gangs, take their cut, and forget your name when a job turns. Netrunners fight in the data behind the walls, and braindances let people live someone else's last hour for a price. The NCPD answers the calls the corporations and gangs cannot settle. There are no levels, classes or status windows here. Nothing in the city runs on magic.
payload.intro: Viktor Vektor's clinic is a converted dental office on a Watson side street, with the reclining chair still bolted to the floor and a sign in the window that buzzes half the time. It is a little after five in the morning, and the street lamps are still on because nobody has told them the night is over. On the steel counter sits a tray of cheap stim patches, and beside it a note in Viktor's square handwriting: find another line of work. He has underlined it twice. Your comm sits face up on the chair arm with three messages waiting. One is from Jackie Welles, a subject line made of exclamation points. One is from the Maelstrom man who calls every morning and signs off with an amount. The last is from Dexter DeShawn, silent since he cut you loose. Viktor comes out of the back, drying his hands from a sink that runs cold. "Read them or don't," he says. "Not in my chair."
starters: Wakako Okada's tea room in Japantown is four tables, a counter of hinoki wood, and a shelf of ceramic cups nobody has been allowed to buy. Rain runs down the window in long streaks, and the neon sign outside turns the water pink, then green. Wakako sits at the back table with a pot of tea that has gone cold, reading a list of names penciled on a sheet of paper. She does not look up when the bell over the door rings. She says your name before you reach the counter, and then she says the price, which she decided before you walked in.

Dexter DeShawn's waiting room in Westbrook is the kind of quiet that costs money. Pale carpet, a fountain nobody has turned on, and a receptionist's desk with no receptionist behind it. A glass wall looks down over the lawns and gates of the district, where security drones hang at their posts like stopped clocks. Dexter's inner door is open. He is at his desk with a comm pressed to one ear, and on the chair across from him sits a folded envelope with your name written on the front in a hand that is not his.

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 22, a small-time merc from Watson who takes whatever a fixer will hand you: scouting, muscle, a quiet pickup. You run with a loose crew of about a dozen people who share a clinic, a bar and a habit of owing each other. Your last job went sideways, your fixer dropped you without a call, and your credstick balance is less than next month's rent. You still have the chrome in your arm.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
Arasaka - The Japanese-founded corporation whose tower dominates the skyline. Wants its cyberware in every body in the city and its rivals forgotten.
Militech - Military hardware and security contracts sold to whoever pays. Wants the city to need its guards a little more every year.
Maelstrom - Chrome-addicted street surgeons who run chop shops and a loan book that never closes. Wants every installment in Watson paid to it, on time.
Valentinos - A gang of mechanics, dancers and drivers who run the clubs and garages on the east edge of Watson. Wants its bars and its respect to stay its own.
NCPD - Night City's police, underpaid and bought by whoever is paying this week. Wants the calls it cannot answer to go away quietly.

entries.title: Night City
entries.content: Night City is a port city of six million people on the Pacific coast, a concrete cage between the water and the Badlands. The megacorps own everything above the twentieth floor. The gangs own what is below it. Everyone else lives in the middle and pays rent to whoever is above them, and the city runs on the gap between what they are owed and what they can pay.

entries.title: Money and chrome
entries.content: Eddies are the money, held on a credstick. Cyberware is cheap to buy and expensive to keep: a clinic quotes the install in eddies and the upkeep in months. Nobody in Watson pays for chrome in full at once. A body with implants is a body that owes someone, and the people who sell it know exactly how much.

entries.title: Names in Night City
entries.content: Night City's names come from everywhere that fed it: Mexican and Salvadoran (Mendes, Ocampo), Nigerian (Adebayo, Oyelaran), Japanese (Okada), Black American and Anglo (Welles, DeShawn, Calloway), old Eastern European (Vektor, Rusk). Most people use a first name or a handle and nobody asks for the rest. Districts keep what they were built as, and blocks are named for the gang that holds them.

entries.title: Watson
entries.content: Watson is the old working district downtown, under the expressways and the rail lines. It has noodle carts, ripperdoc clinics, flophouses and bars that open at dusk and never close. Rents are cheap because the landlords are not paid to fix anything. Maelstrom runs the chrome trade here, the Valentinos drink at the bars on the east edge, and the NCPD patrols in pairs and does not stop.

entries.title: Westbrook
entries.content: Westbrook is the rich district: glass towers, private lawns and gates with security drones at the posts. Corpo families and their staff live here. Anyone from Watson who works in Westbrook is paid in cash that did not come through a Watson bank, and is expected to forget where they were that night. Fixers keep offices here because the money passes through.

entries.title: Pacifica
entries.content: Pacifica was a resort district on the water, built for tourists and abandoned when the money moved uptown. It is a ruin of hotels, flooded lots and gang territory, and the city's dead drop their names there. Nobody goes without a reason and a second weapon. Jobs in Pacifica pay well because the risk does not show on the paperwork.

entries.title: The Badlands
entries.content: The Badlands is the desert outside the city limits: dead towns and dry washes where nomad families and gang crews run convoys across the sand. The corporations cannot reach far into it, which is why people who want to disappear go there. Roads are paid for in cash and water is paid for in favors. Nobody agrees on how far it goes.

entries.title: Arasaka
entries.content: Arasaka is the corporation whose tower dominates the skyline above the twentieth floor. It sells cyberware, security and a promise of order to anyone who can pay. It keeps its own private guards and clinics, and it pays for silence in Watson the way it pays for everything: quietly, in installments, with a name on the paperwork that nobody reads.

entries.title: Militech
entries.content: Militech sells military hardware, armor and security contracts to the corporations, the NCPD and anyone willing to sign a long lease. It wants the city to need it more every year, so it sells armed guards to the people who lost their own. Its agents are polite, expensive and very interested in who was on the Westbrook job.

entries.title: Maelstrom
entries.content: Maelstrom is a gang of chrome addicts and street surgeons who install cyberware in alleys and bill by the month. They run chop shops, unlicensed clinics and a loan book that never closes. A Maelstrom contact will be patient until a payment is late. After that, the chrome they installed begins to hurt.

entries.title: The Valentinos
entries.content: The Valentinos are a gang of mechanics, dancers and drivers who run the clubs and garages on the east edge of Watson. They are loud, loyal and proud of their cars. They respect a deal shaken on the hood of a car and nothing written down. Their bars sell the best drinks in the district and collect the rest in favors.

entries.title: The NCPD
entries.content: The Night City Police Department answers the calls the corporations and gangs cannot settle, and it is underpaid and bought by whoever is paying this week. Patrols run in pairs and do not stop for a Watson street unless someone is dead on it. A report with your name in it follows you into every bank and clinic in the city.

entries.title: Cyberware
entries.content: Cyberware is metal, wire and nerve glued into a body. Reflex boosts, optics and arm frames are sold in a dozen grades, and the cheap grades fail in the rain. Installs are quoted in eddies and every clinic keeps a note on the balance. Removing an implant is possible, but the body rarely forgives the trip.

entries.title: Netrunning
entries.content: Netrunners fight in the data that runs the city: door locks, traffic lights, bank ledgers and the comm networks in a person's own head. They plug in through a cyberdeck, and a bad run can burn the brain behind the implant. A netrunner who works for a fixer is paid in pieces, and the best ones are older than their chrome.

entries.title: Fixers
entries.content: A fixer brings jobs from the corporations and the gangs to merc crews, takes a cut and keeps the names of the people who did the work. A fixer can drop a crew after one bad job without a word, and some will sell the crew's names to the police to close their books. Good fixers keep clean offices in Westbrook. Bad ones are the first people you meet in Watson.

entries.title: Braindances
entries.content: A braindance is a recording of someone's senses, taken from a rig and sold as an experience. People buy a dead man's last hour, a fight, a dance or an affair. Raw recordings are illegal in most of the city and sold openly in Westbrook. A braindance can be a gift, a trap or a confession, and it shows exactly what the seller wanted you to feel.

entries.title: The Afterlife
entries.content: The Afterlife is a bar in Watson where mercs and fixers drink, trade work and make promises they cannot keep. It has a long bar of scarred wood, a jukebox that plays the same six songs, and a back room where gigs are made. The bartender remembers every debt and never says a number out loud.

entries.title: Rent and eddies
entries.content: Rent in Watson is paid weekly, in cash or by credstick, and the landlord keeps a second ledger for the people who are late. Eddies are the currency everyone trusts and nobody has enough of. A merc who makes a good score can clear a debt in a week and lose it all in a month, because the next bill always comes from someone who was counting.

entries.title: The corporate war
entries.content: The corporate wars left the old rivalries in place and the bodies in the ground. Nobody in Watson agrees on how many died, and each corporation's history book gives a different count. The truce is kept by money, and the people who remember the fighting best are paid to keep quiet about it.

world.vibe: Tired, transactional, and cold in the mornings. Everyone quotes a price before they admit a feeling, and nobody says the word debt out loud until they have to.

opening.note: Staged. Beat one: the clinic at five in the morning, the still room and the cold water running in the back. Viktor comes out drying his hands and speaks first, and he says the thing he always says, in fewer words than usual, because he is worried and does not want to show it. He wants you out of the trade before you end up on his table for good. Establish the note on the counter, the stim patches, the comm on the chair arm and the three messages waiting. Keep Viktor dry and exact, never warm in the first beat. Beat two: the comm interrupts. Jackie's call comes in while the player is still in the room, and he is too excited to stop talking. He has a lead, he says, and Dexter has seen the paperwork. Let the Maelstrom man's call come in second, short, quoting a number and nothing else. Dagan Rusk does not explain himself. Beat three: by the third turn the player faces a real choice between taking Jackie's meeting at the Afterlife, going to Pilar Oyelaran's office to settle the rent before the notice goes up, or walking to Wakako Okada's tea room in Japantown, where she has been waiting for someone to ask the right question. Hold Dexter's silence and Wakako's knowledge back until the player asks about the Westbrook job or about who dropped them. Let the morning stay gray and the street lamps stay on.

cast.name: Jackie Welles
cast.role: A merc from the Watson neighborhood who you have crossed paths with on a few jobs. Loud, optimistic and always chasing the next gig. His real partner is a merc named V.
cast.look: Lanky, in a jacket with a cracked band patch on the shoulder, a chrome-plated watch that does not keep time, and a grin he uses to get out of trouble.
cast.manner: Talks with both hands and calls every gig the big one. Never turns down a job before he has heard the price.
cast.secret: He pawned a cyberdeck he borrowed from V to buy into the gig he is pitching, and V does not know yet. If it goes bad, Jackie has nowhere to run.

cast.name: Viktor Vektor
cast.role: Ripperdoc with a clinic on a Watson side street. He patches up half the crews in the district and tells every one of them to find another line of work.
cast.look: Gray at the temples, a neat beard, reading glasses on a cord, and surgeon's hands with a tremor he hides by keeping them busy.
cast.manner: Says the same line at every visit and smooths every dressing flat with his thumb. Never raises his voice, and gets quieter the angrier he is.
cast.secret: For two months he has been paying part of your chrome bill out of his own pocket, and he has quietly paid a Maelstrom collector to keep the balance from rising.

cast.name: Dexter DeShawn
cast.role: Fixer with an office in Westbrook. He sends the best jobs to the crews he likes, and he dropped you after the last one went sideways without calling you once.
cast.look: Tailored charcoal suit, close-cropped silver hair, a slim comm earpiece, and polished shoes that never see Watson mud.
cast.manner: Speaks in the rhythm of a ledger, every sentence a line item. Says 'you know how it is' and means he has already decided. Never gives a straight answer about money.
cast.secret: He gave the NCPD your name as the second shooter on the Westbrook job to keep his own name clean, and the report is already filed.

cast.name: Wakako Okada
cast.role: Fixer in Japantown with a tea room, a stack of pencil-written names and a memory for every job in the city. She sells information more than she sells work.
cast.look: Small and upright, silver hair in a tight knot, a black kimono jacket with worn cuffs, and steady dark eyes behind thin frames.
cast.manner: Speaks in short, clipped sentences and puts a date on everything she tells you, as if it were an invoice. Drinks tea she never finishes.
cast.secret: She has known from the start that the Westbrook job was a Militech setup, and she has been waiting for you to ask the right question so she can sell you the answer.

cast.name: Pilar Oyelaran
cast.role: Landlord of a sagging four-story building in Watson where you rent a unit. She has never fixed the plumbing and has never once missed a rent notice.
cast.look: Broad shoulders under a quilted coat, reading glasses pushed into iron-gray hair, a leather cash pouch at her hip, and a smile that does not reach her eyes.
cast.manner: Treats every complaint as a work order she will get to eventually, and answers each with a story about a worse tenant. Sharpens a pencil with a box cutter while she listens.
cast.secret: She has been paying her own debts to a Valentinos money man with the rent from your building, and she plans to hand the building over to him to clear the rest.

cast.name: Dagan Rusk
cast.role: Maelstrom contact who collects on chrome installed on credit. Polite, patient and in no hurry, until a payment is late.
cast.look: Lean and pale, sunglasses worn at night, a sleeve that hides a chrome forearm, and a faded Maelstrom tattoo at the base of his throat.
cast.manner: Signs off every call with the amount, as other men sign off with a name. Says 'just so we're clear' before every threat, and thanks you for your patience after every one.
cast.secret: The chrome in your arm was stolen from a Militech clinic, and the debt on it is his cover for owing his own boss a far bigger one.

cast.name: Tiv Adebayo
cast.role: Runs a noodle and skewer cart on a Watson corner, open until dawn. She feeds half the crews in the district on credit and remembers who has not paid.
cast.look: Round face, a stained apron over a bright shirt, forearms burned from the grill, and gold studs in both ears that she polishes with her thumb.
cast.manner: Hums while she cooks, usually a tune that never finishes. Hands you an extra skewer for free, then asks for a favor. Mocks anything that costs more than a meal.
cast.secret: She gives the NCPD the cart's schedule so the cart stays open, and she passes Tyger Claws runners' names to the same officers for a cut.

cast.name: V
cast.role: A merc on the rise in Watson who runs jobs with Jackie Welles. Ambitious, sharp and building a name faster than most people build a debt. You have seen V around the Afterlife but never worked together.
cast.look: Lean and alert, a fitted jacket over layered tech-wear, neural port visible at the temple, eyes that scan every doorway before stepping through.
cast.manner: Cocky and direct, always sizing up the room before sitting down. Speaks in short declarative sentences and never asks a question without already knowing the answer. Pockets a small thing from every room, a pen or a matchbook, and forgets it by morning.
cast.secret: A rogue AI fragment lodged in V's cyberware has been making contact, and V has not told anyone, not even Jackie, because the fragment speaks in a dead man's voice.

systems.label: Street Cred
systems.meaning: How Watson and the gangs see you: whether a crew will vouch for you, a fixer will call you back, or a bartender will open the back room.
systems.change: Rises when you finish a job clean, pay a debt in full or keep your name out of a report. Falls when you talk to the NCPD, skip a payment or leave a crew holding the bill.

systems.label: Collector pressure
systems.meaning: How hard the people holding your paper are leaning on you: calls before dawn, a car parked on your block, a visit at the door.
systems.change: Rises when a bill is missed, a new implant goes in on credit, or a collector is seen twice on your street. Falls when you pay down what you owe or do a collector a favor.

systems.label: Heat
systems.meaning: How much attention corporations and gangs pay you: an NCPD flag, a Militech man asking about the Westbrook job, your name in the wrong report.
systems.change: Rises with loud jobs, public fights and a name in a police report. Falls slowly while you stay out of the papers and off the cameras.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How much this person trusts you, as they show you across a counter or a table.
npcSystems.change: Rises when you keep a confidence or pay what you said you would. Falls when you lie to them, give away their name or stand on the wrong side of a deal.

style.art: Neon-soaked cyberpunk noir in ink and airbrush: wet asphalt reflecting magenta and cyan signs, a chrome arm under sodium light, cab headlights smeared through rain, and one figure at the edge of the frame.
style.avoid: Clean corporate sheen, cartoon proportions, bright daylight, and any named character shown in full.

heroes.name: Lark Mendes
heroes.description: A Watson merc dropped by her fixer after a job went wrong. Good with a pistol, bad with money, and still owes for the arm Viktor rebuilt.
heroes.look: Compact and quick, shoulder-length dark hair tied back with wire, a scar through one eyebrow, and a secondhand leather jacket two sizes too big.
heroes.background: Grew up in a Watson flophouse and has worked jobs for Dexter DeShawn for four years. She knows Jackie Welles from the neighborhood and has run a couple of gigs alongside his crew. Her last job in Westbrook went sideways, and her fixer's silence afterward was louder than the gunfire. She owes Viktor Vektor for the arm he rebuilt.
heroes.carries: A pistol with a worn grip, a credstick with forty eddies on it, and a torn Maelstrom receipt.

heroes.name: Bastien Ocampo
heroes.description: Ex-Arasaka security who walked off a Westbrook post and never went back. Now he patches up the crews nobody else will touch.
heroes.look: Tall and broad, close-shaved head with a crescent scar, Arasaka-grade optics he keeps dimmed, and a long black coat over steel-toed boots.
heroes.background: Four years on Arasaka's private security roster in Westbrook, until the night he was ordered to clear a Watson block and walked off the post. Dexter DeShawn gave him muscle work, then dropped him without a call when the Westbrook job went sideways. The chrome in his arm is on credit to Maelstrom, and he has no patience for anyone who thinks a contract is a promise.
heroes.carries: A dimmed Arasaka pass with the name scratched off, and a field medkit.

heroes.name: Nim Calloway
heroes.description: A Westbrook-raised netrunner who learned to burn data in a Pacifica basement. Fast with a cyberdeck, slow to trust the people who pay them.
heroes.look: Slight and sharp-featured, a braided undercut, a rig of cables across one shoulder, and a cracked comm screen covered in stickers from bands that stopped touring.
heroes.background: Raised in Westbrook by a housekeeper while their parents worked corporate hours. Left for Pacifica as soon as they could sign their own lease and taught themselves to run data on salvaged decks. Dexter DeShawn hired them for runs, then dropped them when the Westbrook job went sideways. The port at their temple went in on credit, and Maelstrom wants its money.
heroes.carries: A cyberdeck with a cracked casing, three spare chips and a stolen Militech access badge.
